newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Codelco delays power stake sale until 1998.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Codelco delays power stake sale until 1998.

text.p: Chile's state copper company Codelco has postponed the sale of its 35 percent stake in the Tocopilla power plant until next year, said Codelco's finance and administration vice president Albert Cussen.
"It is likely that it will be best to wait until the natural gas project and the new plants which the Norgas group is planning are underway," Cussen told a news conference.
"The sale of the shares is unlikely to take place before early 1998."
Codelco had planned to sell its shareholding this year through the sale of shares in the local and international markets.

Tocopilla, which was privatized last year and renamed Electroandina, is heading the Norgas consortium, which plans to build a natural gas pipeline to bring gas from Argentina across the Atacama Desert to northern Chile.
Electroandina is owned by a group including Spain's Iberdrola SA, Belgium's Powerfin SA and Chilean firm Enagas.
Tocopilla is the largest power generator in northern Chile and supplies power to the region's booming mining industry.
The natural gas project includes building a new combined cycle gas-fired plant as well as the conversion of the existing coal fired plant to gas.
